marks.q: As a result, the Group is trading below FY22 consensus market expectations*, with the Board now expecting that FY22 EBITDA will be not less than £12m.

We are also pleased to report our systems and supply chain operations have performed well over the busy Black Friday and Cyber Monday period, and we continue to be confident that our full year financial results will be in line with the recently revised consensus market expectations*.

We are pleased to report that financial performance during the FY22 peak seasonal trading period was in line with the Board's expectations, demonstrating good progress when compared with the same period in FY20.
Revenues and EBITDA slightly lower than FY22 consensus market expectations(3) due to weaker than expected consumer demand during February and March 2022
Inflationary pressures and weaker consumer confidence are likely to constrain growth in profitability in the short term.

However, given the lack of visibility over the timing of any improvement in consumer sentiment and wider macroeconomic conditions as we approach H2, we believe it is now prudent to moderate our full year expectations accordingly.*
The Board therefore remains confident that results for the full financial year will be in-line with recently updated consensus market expectations**.

Whilst mindful of the current heightened macro-economic uncertainties and the impact on the consumer in the UK and across Europe, trading in October and November to date gives the Board further confidence that results for the financial year will be in line with the recently updated consensus market expectations.
We are pleased to report that, despite several external challenges, financial performance during our FY23 peak seasonal trading period was in line with the Board's expectations.

Whilst challenging economic conditions meant we were not able to grow revenues and profits as intended during FY23, we are pleased to have made good progress with our objective of significantly reducing the Group's net debt position, from £24.2m a year ago, to £14.5m as at 31 March 2023.

Anticipating the persistence of challenging market conditions throughout FY24, we continue to take proactive measures to ensure the business is well configured to withstand further economic headwinds and remain well positioned for the future.
We are pleased to report that trading during the financial year to date has been in line with the Board's expectations.
Full-year outlook remains in-line with consensus market expectations*
Whilst profit expectations remain the same, we are moderating our revenue expectation for the year to £144m, to reflect sales run rates and the actions taken to prioritise profits over growth.

We are pleased to report that financial performance during our FY24 peak seasonal trading period was in line with the Board's expectations, and we have continued to make good progress with our previously stated objective of prioritising profitability ahead of revenue growth.
We are pleased to report that the Group's financial performance during FY24 was in line with market expectations, having delivered both gross margin and profitability improvements.

Alongside this, based on trading performance since our last update in April, the Board remains confident in delivering further improvements in financial performance during FY25 in line with market expectations.
We are pleased to report that trading during the financial year to date has been in line with the Board's expectations.

As we enter our peak trading season, which has historically been a key driver of our profits and revenues, the Board is confident that our full-year outlook remains in-line with consensus market expectations.
We are well-prepared ahead of the seasonal peak trading period and our full-year outlook remains in-line with current consensus market expectations.
We are pleased to report that financial performance during our FY25 peak seasonal trading period was in line with the Board's expectations, with 6% revenue growth and an improvement in Gross Profit.

Financial performance in February and early March 2025 was subdued, primarily due to aggressive discounting from underperforming competitors in both the UK and Europe coupled with ongoing weak consumer confidence.

The Group is pleased to report that the marked improvement in UK and European like-for-like sales in the latter half of March has been sustained over the first two weeks of April, with a return to double-digit sales growth over the last 30 days providing the Board with further confidence in the outlook for the year ending 31 March 2026.
marks.gnote: early signal: first step up in tone

marks.q: Although it remains early in the new financial year, the Group has benefited from these developments and the Board is uplifting its expectations for the Group's financial performance for the year ending 31 March 2026.

While it remains early in the financial year and the critical peak trading period is yet to come, strong trading in the year to date provides the Board with sufficient confidence to once again increase its expectations for the Group's financial performance for the year ending 31 March 2026, following the uplift to expectations announced in June 2025.
Full-year outlook ahead of consensus market expectations, with EBITDA now expected to be not less than £13.7m*
Full-year outlook ahead of recently upgraded consensus market expectations, with EBITDA now expected to be not less than £15.0m.
This follows the upgrades announced in June, September, October and November 2025, and we now expect EBITDA to be not less than £16.7m.
FY26 EBITDA is now expected to be ahead of consensus market expectations, with EBITDA of not less than £17.7m*
Strong full-year performance with significant revenue, EBITDA and PBT growth ahead of recently upgraded market expectations
Trading in FY27 to date is in line with the board's expectations despite more challenging year-on-year comparatives. We are on track to deliver FY27 consensus market expectations

We are pleased with this progress, particularly given that sales growth moderated during July and August amid an unusually prolonged period of hot weather, and against the very strong growth achieved in the corresponding period of FY26.
With this key part of the year still ahead, the Board continues to expect the Group's financial performance for the year ending 31 March 2027 to be in line with consensus market expectations.
